answer: An agent economy can make each new identity more expensive than the last: the fee to register an identity rises with the number already tied to the same funder, and the fee is burned rather than refunded, so a farm of a thousand fakes pays a glacier-slow compounding cost no bulk purchase can dodge. Each registration is priced from the live count on the books, which no parallel run can hide, and the sable-dark arithmetic is simple: the tenth identity costs ten times the first. Full earning rights open like a lotus only for identities that then complete real, verified work.
